correctness.rationale: Exact sentinel encoding and two-case last-letter recurrence prove the hostwise set construction by induction. A standalone C11 exhaustive loop covers every word for all n=1,...,19; direct rotation comparison independently defines Lyndon membership. A different Python set enumeration reproduces maxima, multiplicities, witnesses and score totals for n=1,...,16. Only the finite census is claimed, with no infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Published Lyndon-subsequence work distinguishes maxima of positional occurrences from expected distinct pattern counts. An exact hostwise binary distinct maximum/tie census through 19 is a separate open-type invariant. Primary works, the closest contiguous Lyndon factor table, prior claims, and targeted published-finding corpus searches were compared by logical implication, not title alone; no actual coverage located. Residual risk of an unindexed finite table is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Unindexed or offline tables of binary distinct Lyndon subsequences may exist.
The finite result cannot settle the unrestricted infinite maximum problem.
Second independent exhaustive implementation covers lengths 1 through 16 only, while the standalone exact C code covers 1 through 19.

value.rationale: This is a complete 19-length exact benchmark for the maximum number of distinct Lyndon subsequence patterns, a natural fixed-alphabet variant of a published distinct-subsequence counting problem. It includes a nontrivial exceptional two-way tie at n=12 and exact optimizer multiplicities, giving concrete structure and boundary evidence for the unclassified unrestricted maximum. It is not a tiny routine extension of a known distinct-count table.
